title: Pvt Ltd vs LLP: The Ultimate Guide for Indian Founders (2024)
excerpt: Confused between Private Limited and LLP? We break down the liability, compliance, and fundraising differences to help you decide.

sections.heading: What is a Private Limited Company?
paragraphs: Choosing the right business structure is the foundation of your entrepreneurial journey. In India, the two most popular entities for organized businesses are the Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd) and the Limited Liability Partnership (LLP). Making the wrong choice can lead to unnecessary compliance burdens or missed fundraising opportunities.

A Pvt Ltd company is a separate legal entity held by shareholders. It is the gold standard for startups looking to raise venture capital or offer ESOPs to employees. It is governed effectively by the Companies Act, 2013.

sections.heading: What is an LLP?
paragraphs: An LLP is a balanced structure that offers the limited liability of a company and the operational flexibility of a partnership. It is governed by the LLP Act, 2008, and is ideal for professional service firms and small businesses not seeking external equity funding.
Whether you choose an LLP or a Pvt Ltd, Pelago Consultants handles the entire incorporation process—from name reservation (RUN/Spice+) to the final Certificate of Incorporation.
• Registration Cost: LLPs are approximately 30-40% cheaper to incorporate than Pvt Ltd companies.
• Compliance Burden: Pvt Ltd companies must conduct mandatory audits. LLPs only require an audit if turnover exceeds ₹40 Lakhs or capital contribution exceeds ₹25 Lakhs.
• Fundraising: VCs prefer Pvt Ltd companies as they allow for the easy issuance of shares. LLPs cannot issue equity shares.
• Taxation: Both are taxed at a flat rate of 30% (plus cess), but Pvt Ltd companies can opt for a lower 25% or 15% rate under specific sections if conditions are met.

title: How to Save Taxes with Startup India Registration (DPIIT)
excerpt: Did you know recognized startups can get a 3-year tax holiday? Learn how to leverage Section 80-IAC and angel tax exemptions.

sections.heading: 1. Section 80-IAC: The 3-Year Tax Holiday
paragraphs: The "Startup India" initiative is more than just a badge; it's a fiscal bazooka for early-stage companies. However, simply getting a DPIIT recognition number isn't enough to save tax. You need to apply specifically for exemptions.
Recognized startups can apply for a full deduction of their profits for any 3 consecutive years out of the first 10 years of incorporation.
• Must be a Private Limited Company or LLP.
• Incorporated after April 1, 2016.
• Must validate "Innovation" or "Scalability" to the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB).

sections.heading: 2. Angel Tax Exemption (Section 56(2)(viib))
paragraphs: Startups often raise funds at a premium. Previously, this premium was taxed as income. With DPIIT recognition and a specific declaration (Form 2), startups are exempt from this levy, making fundraising smoother.
Self-certification for labor laws, relaxed public procurement norms, and faster winding up are additional operational benefits that save indirect costs.

Trademarks are filed under specific "Classes" (1-45). For example:

title: Unlock Collateral-Free Loans with Udyam (MSME) Registration
excerpt: The Udyam Registration is a gateway to government subsidies, lower interest rates, and protection against delayed payments.

sections.heading: Top Financial Benefits
paragraphs: Government definition of "Small Business" has expanded. Now, even companies with turnover up to ₹250 Crores can be classified as Medium Enterprises. The Udyam Registration portal is the only official way to register as an MSME.
Under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust, MSMEs can avail loans without giving external security (like land or property). The government acts as the guarantor.
Many banks offer ROI which is 1% to 1.5% lower than standard business loan rates for Udyam holders.
This is a powerful legal tool. If a buyer does not pay you within 45 days, they are liable to pay compound interest at 3 times the RBI bank rate. You can file a case with the MSME Samadhaan council.

title: One Person Company (OPC): The Solopreneur's Best Legal Structure
excerpt: Want limited liability but define yourself as a solo founder? OPC gives you the best of both worlds without needing a co-founder.

sections.heading: What is an OPC?
paragraphs: For the longest time, a solo entrepreneur had to settle for a Proprietorship, which meant unlimited liability. If the business failed, personal assets were at risk. The One Person Company (OPC) changed that game.
An OPC is a legitimate Private Limited Company with only **one shareholder** and **one director** (who can be the same person). It provides the corporate veil of limited liability to solo founders.
• Limited Liability: Your personal savings and assets are safe even if the business incurs losses.
• Corporate Status: Easier to get bank loans and vendor trust compared to a proprietorship.
• Succession: You must appoint a "Nominee" who takes over in case of the owner's incapacitation, ensuring business continuity.

title: Is a Partnership Firm Right for Your Small Business?
excerpt: Traditional partnership firms are easy to start and distinct from LLPs. Learn when to choose this classic structure.

sections.heading: Registered vs Unregistered Partnership
paragraphs: Before LLPs and Startups, there was the Partnership Firm. It remains a popular choice for small, unorganized businesses, home runs specific trades, or family-run shops where legal complexity needs to be zero.
You can run a partnership simply on a deed (contract). However, registering it with the Registrar of Firms (ROF) is highly recommended.
It is the cheapest and fastest way for 2+ people to start a business. Compliance is minimal—no annual filing with the MCA, only Income Tax Returns are needed.
• Legal Rights: An unregistered firm cannot file a case against a third party (like a client refusing to pay) to enforce a contract.
• Partner Disputes: Partners cannot legally sue each other or the firm in an unregistered setup.

title: The Essential Post-Incorporation Compliance Checklist
excerpt: Registered your company? The work just started. Essential list of compliances to handle within 30 days of incorporation.

sections.heading: The First 30-Day Checklist
paragraphs: Congratulations on your Certificate of Incorporation! But don't pop the champagne just yet. The Companies Act imposes immediate duties on new directors. Missing these can lead to heavy penalties or even "Strike Off".
You must appoint a Chartered Accountant as your statutory auditor within 30 days. This is not optional, even if you have zero revenue.
Open a current account in the company's name. You will need your COI, PAN, and MOA/AOA.
Shareholders must transfer the subscription money (as mentioned in the MOA) to this new bank account.
Within 180 days, you must file Form INC-20A proving that the capital has been deposited. You cannot legally start business operations or borrow money without this.

title: Digital Signature Certificate (DSC): Why Every Director Needs One
excerpt: The DSC is the digital equivalent of a handwritten signature. Understand its classes, uses, and security importance.

sections.heading: What is it used for?
paragraphs: In the digital India ecosystem, physical signatures are obsolete for corporate filings. A **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** is a secure USB token containing your encrypted signature data.
Currently, Class 3 is the standard. It provides the highest level of security and verification. Both the Director and the Authorized Signatory need a valid DSC.
• Company Incorporation: Signing the SPICe+ forms.
• GST Filings: Authorizing monthly returns.
• Income Tax: Verifying ITRs.
• Tenders: Determining identity in e-auctions.

title: How to Start an Import-Export Business: IEC Code Guide
excerpt: Taking your business global? The Import Export Code (IEC) is your passport to international trade.

sections.heading: Who Needs It?
paragraphs: You cannot import goods into India or export services/goods out of India without a 10-digit number known as the **Import Export Code (IEC)**.
Even service providers (like freelancers getting paid in USD) need an IEC to avail benefits under schemes like SEIS (Service Exports from India Scheme).
• Importers: To clear customs and send money abroad.
• Exporters: To send shipments and receive foreign currency into their bank accounts.
• Validity: Lifetime. No renewal needed.
• Compliance: An annual update (KYC) is mandatory between April and June every year, even if no trades occurred.

sections.heading: Purpose of the Act

It regulates the working conditions of employees, including:

title: FSSAI License: A Complete Guide for Food Businesses
excerpt: From home bakers to large restaurants, FSSAI registration is mandatory to ensure food safety and consumer trust.

sections.heading: Types of Licenses
paragraphs: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) ensures that the food products we consume are safe. Every Food Business Operator (FBO) must obtain this license.
The license depends on your turnover and scale:
Displaying your 14-digit FSSAI number on your packaging and premises is mandatory by law.
• Basic Registration: For petty food businesses with turnover < ₹12 Lakhs/year.
• State License: For medium businesses with turnover between ₹12 Lakhs and ₹20 Crores.
• Central License: For large manufacturers, importers, or e-commerce players with turnover > ₹20 Crores.

title: Retain Top Talent: How to Structure an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP)
excerpt: Startups often cannot match corporate salaries. ESOPs allow you to attract talent by offering them a slice of ownership.

sections.heading: Key Terms to Know
paragraphs: An **Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP)** gives employees the right to buy company shares at a future date at a pre-determined price. It aligns the employee's success with the company's success.
Pelago helps you draft the ESOP policy and manage the "Cap Table" to ensure you don't dilute too much equity accidentally.
• Grant Date: When the option is given to the employee.
• Vesting Period: The minimum time an employee must work before they earn the right to the shares (usually 1-4 years).
• Exercise Price: The discounted price at which the employee buys the shares.

title: Starting a Non-Profit? Guide to Section 8 Company Registration
excerpt: Section 8 companies are the most trusted form of NGOs in India. Learn about the process and charitable privileges.

sections.heading: Why Section 8 over Trust?
paragraphs: If your objective is art, science, charity, or social welfare, a **Section 8 Company** is the modern alternative to Trusts and Societies. It operates like a limited company but cannot pay dividends to members.
Like other NGOs, Section 8 companies can apply for 12A (Income Tax Exemption) and 80G (Donor Tax Benefit) registrations to attract more donations.
• Credibility: Being regulated by the Central Govt (MCA) gives it higher credibility with donors and CSR funding agencies.
• Structure: It has a clearer legal structure regarding management and ownership.

title: Nidhi Company Registration: Starting a Lending Business
excerpt: A Nidhi Company enables you to start a loan business within a closed group of members without needing an RBI license.

sections.heading: The Business Model
paragraphs: Starting a bank or NBFC requires massive capital (min ₹2-10 Crores). A **Nidhi Company** is a unique class of NBFC that deals only with its members and requires much less capital (starts with ₹10 Lakhs).
The core principle is mutual benefit. Nidhi companies accept deposits from members and lend to members.
• Loans: Secured loans (Gold, Property, Deposits) are safer.
• Restrictions: They cannot advertise to the general public or deal with anyone who is not a member (shareholder).

title: Business Pivots: How to Legally Change Your Company Name
excerpt: Rebranding? Changing your company name involves a legal procedure with the ROC. Here is the step-by-step process.

sections.heading: The Process
paragraphs: Startups pivot. Maybe your old name doesn't fit your new vision. Changing a company name is legal, but it requires approval from the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
Once approved, you get a new Certificate of Incorporation. Remember to update your PAN, GST, and Bank Accounts immediately after the change!
• Board Resolution: Approve the new name idea.
• Name Reservation: Apply via 'RUN' (Reserve Unique Name) facility on MCA.
• EGM: Hold an Extraordinary General Meeting to pass a special resolution.
• Filing: File MGT-14 and INC-24 with the Central Government.

title: Fast Track Exit: How to Legally Close a Private Limited Company
excerpt: Closing a business is as important as starting one. Use the FTE (Fast Track Exit) mode to close an inactive company cleanly.

sections.heading: Eligibility for FTE
paragraphs: If a business fails, leaving the company "dormant" is dangerous because penalties will accumulate. The **Fast Track Exit (FTE)** scheme allows defunct companies to shut down without a lengthy winding-up process.
This is the application form for strike-off. It must be accompanied by an indemnity bond from directors and a statement of accounts certifying zero liabilities.
• The company has not started business within 1 year of incorporation.
• OR, the company has been inactive for the last 2 financial years.
• The company has no assets and no liabilities.

This contains your Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account, and Director's Report. It must be filed within 30 days of the AGM.
This details shareholding structure, changes in directorship, and meetings held. It must be filed within 60 days of the AGM.
